### Chunk0091 save hunks and current absent-inventory reconciliation checkpoint, 2026-10-09

- All55 assigned frozen save implementation/interface hunks now physically read in bounded untruncated outputs: save.c47-61,62-78,79-91 and save.h1-10. Together with previous whole added policy/interface this covers all57 assigned hunks. Whole frozen assigned ranges are identity scope, not an extra claim of reading every unchanged save line
- Complete frozen-to-current unified3 deltas for both save paths read, with exact hunk hashes and SequenceMatcher line mapping below. Current save.c2313/header260 differ from frozen due fresh ship initialization, mine-specific absent key handling,10-entry live absent cache distinct from16 disk capacity, absent record refresh/eviction, pending restored-inventory retention and post-barrier connected-player grants. Original handmade comments preserved; stale ordering prose is not code repair
- Current metadata reader validates exact version/footer/payload arithmetic and checksum streaming before campaign decoding and gear staging. Campaign bytes required; optional gear discard permitted on ordinary disk load, prohibited restoring world/source. Pending states cleared on entry; successful candidate campaign transferred only at success, buffers freed and file position restored. Source/world caller failure rollback and semantic gear admission remain to trace before judging transaction completeness
- Current absent cache prefers client ID and permits callsign fallback only if one ID absent; current metadata lookup still falls back by callsign even with two distinct IDs. Metadata reader counts bound8 active/16 absent, while live remember caps10 and hands evicted inventory to recovery owner. The disagreement requires actual transport/identity and canonical BR0388 acceptance tracing; no independent identity defect admitted yet
- Record apply clamps weapon selection/afterburner, stores omega through recovery, replaces durable flags and adds same-level keys; bounded paired ammo arrays and self object shield mirror. Actual native apply caller admission still pending, no all-scalar or arbitrary slot safety proof
- Autosave guards briefing/travel/restore/transfer, live coop/window/player state and countdown policy; rotates slot only after save success and restores game ID/callsign on returned failure. Underlying stop_time/save close outcome and paired scheduler ownership need caller trace, not an assumed new root. Zero-initialized JSON string buffers do not fix raw escaping; existing GQF0182 retained
- Progress inventory exact version5/count/length/checksum and explicit flush/close precede checked temp/backup publication; backup recovery failure can still be ignored, so no atomic or interruption acceptance credited. Current loader stages copied recovery data before mission/level/record/host admission. set_pending changes pending storage, not live ledger; apply_pending resets/rebuilds live ledger and deliberately discards invalid optional rows while returning1. ### Chunk0101 robot admission and summary publication checkpoint, 2026-10-09

Whole236-line RobotPreviewRequestStore validates supported game, scanned source row, robot membership and owned cache generation. Creation filters successful rows, builds typed navigation entries and requires the selected item index; launch checks nonempty/nonnegative/distinct robot_numbers and selected membership, then navigation index bounds, nonnegative robot/nonblank level for every entry, and selected robot/level equality. Activity onCreate calls this validator before its native worker. Missing duplicate native index validation alone does not prove an ordinary invalid-index launch; arbitrary malformed-native requests remain deferred

Native selection reads count/active and queues pending index atomically. The draw handler consumes it and may load another level, reload D2 robot tables, update camera/palette and configure robot/behavior before assigning navigation index. Activity immediately labels the requested robot and posts a summary read100ms later, or reads it immediately after enabling attack. JNI calls android_robot_preview_attack_summary directly on that UI path; native summary traverses mutable Robot_preview_number, Robot_info, Weapon_info, behavior, sub-flags and difficulty. Initial active release/acquire publishes initialization but does not synchronize subsequent engine-owned navigation and table changes. A fixed100ms delay is not acknowledgement or a coherent generation. Extend existing OPEN BR0029 engine ownership/snapshot acceptance, no duplicate finding and no newly asserted race on the summary string itself: only its UI writer was found

Actual behavior/role/channel names and summary literals are ASCII with numeric formatting; no user robot label or source filename enters the summary. NewStringUTF alone therefore does not establish a new standard-UTF8 producer failure here. Retain GQR0170 C ABI/JNI allocation and first-exception ownership; the std::string result and typed JSON work are outside the request stream parse catch. Keep existing GQR0212 admission/work budgets and GQR0102 immutable source generation. BR0588 request correlation and BR0654 incomplete render-probe retry remain future fixture acceptance, not fresh device results

Future BR0029 acceptance: compute an owned immutable summary on the engine thread after successful robot/level application; publish request/session, applied selection sequence, robot/level and summary together with explicit synchronization. UI must distinguish requested from applied state and accept only its current acknowledged generation. Never solve this with another fixed delay or a mutex around only the formatting string while engine tables remain mutable. Barrier-schedule actual main-looper summary reads and rapid navigation/attack toggles against draw consumption, paired D1/D2 cross-level robot-table replacement, loading failure and close/recreation. Require no mutable engine access on UI, no races/invalid access, coherent robot-label/summary identity, truthful pending/failure outcome and rejection of stale callbacks. Runtime/race/allocation/resource/malformed/security execution remains deferred

All four analysis gates now have saved source/consumer/fixture evidence; final owner normalization, immutable report/import and independent verification still pending.0101 remains TODO, no GQC/GQD/terminal rank admitted, no new finding/status/inherited saving and no product/test/script mutation. ### Chunk0102 edge progress and confirmation consumer checkpoint, 2026-10-09

Current whole410-line edge/99-line header/51-line C interface read; all assigned sources equal frozen head. Both D1/D2 CMake lists include shared snapshot/edge/planner. Confirmation actor/result source is D2-only and automation explicitly rejects D1; absence of D1 actor hooks is not a missing parity implementation

Edge validates segment/side/reciprocal child, excludes exit side before flyable, preserves directional locks even for legacy progress and excludes unlock-only opener from fired shortcut. Effective wall state uses authoritative progress or shootable-trigger topology; fallback reads snapshot. Snapshot derives opened from actual opened flag or opening/cloaking callback; it is not equivalent to locked=false. Ordered trigger actions and terminal-exit precedence are explicit. Progress keeps one-shot consumption, avoided trigger/remote-wall masks and predicted kind/lock/open fields; native apply checks valid/disabled/consumed trigger and excludes paired lock/unlock effects. No synthetic state vector/schema malformed probe or new per-index root

Remote edge admission requires enabled capability, valid unlocked opposite face, admitted key and nonavoided wall, then emits prerequisite rather than immediate passage. Actual dependency planner enables capability only with wall_shootable callback; searches pre-opening reachable positions, optional detailed/door aim and guided alternatives, and checks actual shot prerequisite. Failed remote attempt restores saved dependency state and avoids that remote wall; this is not an unconditionally reachable opposite-face shortcut

Focused native fixture1480-1585 checks ordered wall transitions, directional one-sided lock/unlock in authoritative=false/true with opened=false, reveal rearm and consumed one-shot rejection. This is not acceptance for every temporarily opened/closing locked face. Keep opening/closing/fired-opener state matrix and real live-route downstream revalidation under existing BR0335 acceptance before interpreting transient passage as permanently authorized. No new ordinary failure admitted from a hand-constructed state alone

Whole54-line Counterstrike open/locked script checks two confirmed routes, exact objective labels and frame/simulation RNG repeat equality. Whole50-line Lostlvls directional script regenerates isolated metadata, checks ordinary non-guided door prerequisite, actual flare wall/segment log, no fallback/guided label, full player radius, complete sequence, identical JSON and normalized agreement. Whole47-line Obsidian remote script checks actual off-segment flare log, full sequence, JSON-repeat equality and normalized agreement. They declare test_guidebot_route_regressions ownership; catalog registration search is discovery only pending actual owner runner/catalog read. Native CTest target/source and registration snippets physically read; no execution

Whole34-line expanded-door plan records historical corpus17missions/343levels, general EAF2 firing-access fix and paired builds/demo/Android validation. It explicitly defers live/co-op reproduction to user logs and does not establish fresh runtime acceptance here. Prior0087 narrative recovered without JSON truncation; six relevant existing physical bindings unchanged and reusable as retained prior evidence only. Prior0070 headless narrative establishes known terminal start/failure/native transition and output publication owners but no new full route implementation credit

MSVC route_planner_c.h now has balanced push8/pop immediately around its summary. Preserve this source repair; OPEN BR0229 broader default/pack1/pack16/include-order/C-versus-C++/paired-header sentinel acceptance still unexecuted. Search found input-demo packing fixtures, not demonstrated route-header fixtures; no new packing defect/status closure or restored leaked packing

Confirmation assigned tail clamps timeout1..3600 and speed100..200 and prevents key/exit/speed config during RUNNING. Actor-specific velocity scaling precedes smoothing in actual D2 aipath; drive hook runs before ordinary AI. Drive follows live dropped key position and keeps real shot visibility/full-radius target-leg checks distinct from waypoint nearness. Status summary is borrowed engine-owned state, not an immutable cross-thread snapshot solely because returned const; actual automation and introspection consumers are engine-side named context, not a demonstrated new UI race

Recorded confirmation startup requires local single-player, initializes seed/ticks, creates actor at authored/restored pose, uses at least player radius, deliberately sandboxes player/ordinary robots and selects live goal. Fail stores terminal status/problem/RNG and restores player. Fixed60Hz tick remainder and simulation-time/frame/no-progress/replan bounds are source logic, not whole wall-clock deadline proof. Frontier wait/extension does not itself complete semantic objective

Exit action checks authored crossing or one-sided target touch then calls normal trigger handler. D2 switch validates wall/trigger, intercepts requested/ordinary confirmation exit before normal dispatch; final-boss hook runs only after dead boss/control-center/countdown checks. Assigned requested exit rejects different trigger, suppresses normal transition to serialize result, and separate run_exit_transition requires confirmed actor pose and actual native level change. Native switch can also receive weapon-parent shot dispatch; final proof still needs complete call provenance/shot/disabled/exit admission reconciliation, not a blanket physical crossing claim from callback signature. ### Chunk0105 actual synth backend and paired HUD consumer checkpoint, 2026-10-09

Nine fresh source/plan physical bindings below. Unchanged HEAD8a730eb6aa1d34382b4a76e6f1f5abd3e18aa96c, no product/test/script edit, runtime/media/device/build/fault execution, canonical new finding or inherited saving.0105TODO, only firstgatecomplete

Current music_synth.cpp owns music_fluid SF2 plus FM, not the pinned TinySoundFont runtime. Its hmp_begin/capture/control wrapper delegates SF2 to the music_fluid object; FM uses separate controller handling. Therefore hmp_tsf_state.h TSF-specific getter compensation must be validated for actual offline/helper/test TSF consumers separately from active FluidSynth state. Existing earlier synth/backend repairs cannot be reopened merely because the assigned historical header name retains tsf

Whole music_synth_hmp.h actual conversion owner read: choose FM HMQ substitute when supplied; call device-specific converter. FM conversion failure or synth rejection frees converted MIDI, zeros outputs, prepares fallback synth and reconverts original HMP through GM selection. This preserves arrangement provenance rather than applying FM events directly to SF2. Need music_synth_prepare/is_fm/fm_sequence/acceptance and actual digi/preview timeline ranges/lifetime next; no actual fallback/device/media execution inferred from the wrapper

HMP114-219 current legacy track converter read closes prior1-114/220-290 gaps. Delta conversion bounded to four bytes; metadata length/payload checks and exact terminal EOT; supported channel event widths/running-status emission. Branch-aware playback is separate. Whole-current HMP credit still not claimed from unchanged assigned diff hunk; physical291-710 is frozen complete hunk evidence, not a fresh current whole-source read

Offline midi_tsf_render55-78/118-160 dispatch uses hmp_tsf_control, optional context-prefix capture/reset/begin before target prefix and finite timeline; rendering requires every block to fill. Actual test_midi_seek_timeline260-378 checks finite loop end silence, retained preset/bank/pan/full-scale LSB/volume after reset/CC121, pan endpoints/LSB update and invokes state test from main only after actual soundfont file loads. Wrong argc or unreadable font errors rather than ordinary pass. Source assertions not executed and not proof of FluidSynth backend acceptance. Pinned TSF/getter/setter dependency source and build registration still pending

Paired gauges named callers read. get_pnum_for_hud selects Current_obs_player only under observer/is_observing_player, otherwise Player_num; the callee alone does not admit arbitrary indices. HUD preference gates whole block; competitive multiplayer excludes block unless COOP/ROBOTS; timer follows network PlayTimeAllowed and control-center state; shared robot/hostage/secret draw and right-inset natural hook retained. Need observer admission and actual cooperative hostage update/disconnect/world counts before any root claim

Whole maintained coop_hostage_hud plan confirms intentional team aggregate and authenticated Android status fields, focused native HUD/layout/paired builds historical only; live multiplayer pickup/death explicitly unrun. Whole D2 preference investigation says per-pilot flag defaults0 and launcher can display another pilot's preference, also statusbar/rearview/HUD_toolong gates; no source fix in that historical pass. Do not reinstate removed secret-only mode or bypass preference from assumed expectation. Need actual draw boundary and maintained HUD/native/shipstatus fixtures before terminal acceptance

First mixed read requested music_synth375-420 beyond actual412 and stopped after displaying375-412; recovered pending offline/test/plan reads explicitly with valid bounds. Missing android/CMakeLists and Windows glob rg failure are discovery errors, no product finding/read credit. Preview diff replaces private ring with shared pcm_ring and TSF calls with music_synth FluidSynth/ymfm. Adds renderer effects/soundfont replacement, bank callback boundedname/catalog entries, HMP conversion/info/state restore/capture, sample-rate8000..96000 and shared playback levels. Successful replacement stops/joins rendering then closes old synth; failed preparation preservesold by headercontract, need unchanged surrounding control locks/failure paths. Diagnosticopt-in counts callback/underrun/consumption and firstnonzerosample; default no scans/perchunkclocks in new diagnostic branches. Timing instrumentation is not an audio oracle and callback-optin overhead must not be described as absent

Seek queues integer-ms target atomically, renderthread exchanges it then resets synth/restores initialHMPstate, replays logical controllers/program/pitch/note+sustain bookkeeping and restarts soundingnotes withenvelopes. Changes ring under resetmutex; publishes position/duration atomicfields. Header explicitly approximate seek and acceptedrequest semantics, not rendered-PCM equivalence. Future caller/fixture diagnosis must preserve that acceptedpolicy rather than reopen exact waveform reconstruction merely for envelope restart. Per-fieldatomic playback snapshots do not themselves prove coherent multi-fieldgeneration. Source cache/indexkeybound upstream TML admission remains to trace, no malformed probe/new issue from castalone

Finite seek range adds repeat_event/repeat_frame/end_frame; validates positive sample rate/end and0<=repeat<end, framequantization mustyieldstart<end. Render wraps clock/cursor only if repeatevent, capsnext/event boundary toend, avoids dispatchingdueatfiniteend; explicitly preserves synthcontrollers/voices. Preview currentlysetsNULLrepeat/finiteHMPend by changed reset function; inspect complete scheduler/render/caller flow and existing HMP repeatquantization/state owners before duplicatefinding. Int-ms semantics and renderer equivalence need actual current fixture oracles

First source gate complete; remaining metadata consumers/current whole preview/scheduler/JNI/UI/fixtures/owners then immutable report/import/terminal audit. No fresh wholecurrentread credit from byteequality. Globalpreflights/sweeps/investigations/current-head/worktree/finalclosure remain required

        "line_lf_sha256": "14d82d042414885fd8344769e5d1b9203c5362b859b1cbd5ef5e84c2e162a9e9"
      },
      {
        "line": 13488,
        "text": "- Expected: `HEADLESS-RUN OK` and exit zero are emitted only after every replay frame completes, every required output is written and closed, and the selected embedded-result comparison succeeds; every other terminal outcome emits `HEADLESS-RUN FAIL` and exits nonzero.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "9d7d1a20ee6558665fd94ac50a4d2c730a049c11d7b37c89f2b519ae87507d1c"
      },
      {
        "line": 13489,
        "text": "- Suggested fix: Propagate a typed replay outcome through stepping and finishing, including frame completion, result-write, and comparison status. Have the headless main retain the first failure, avoid converting an interrupted loaded session into success, print the matching failure reason, and return nonzero. Keep the wrapper's independent comparison as defense in depth.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "d403f1c610e3a8ce5b092cf75dec0b662d237c9d246229b5ef272cb8587bf14c"
      },
      {
        "line": 13490,
        "text": "- Additional suggested fix (R1-CHUNK-0268): Capture the observed cursor, current `GameTime64`, terminal kind, and immutable terminal snapshot before unloading, and write those observed values without consulting the loaded final-frame aggregate. Define only the specific post-transition fields that cannot be compared, rather than copying them from actual into expected. Require a terminal exit to occur at the recorded frame boundary and clock before any subset comparison can pass.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "9b818a10dadbedd22828adde67272952767afd4324c3779229866614b9330373"
      },
      {
        "line": 13491,
        "text": "- Validation: Add headless process tests for successful exact replay plus injected prepare, direct-command, RNG-restore, actual-result-write, state-trace start, write, flush, and close, and embedded-result-mismatch failures. Assert only the exact replay with all requested outputs complete returns zero and prints `HEADLESS-RUN OK`; every failure must return nonzero, print `HEADLESS-RUN FAIL`, and remain a failure through the PowerShell wrapper.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "e6eb81b08107ca883f36bca653bfd5d9a894a531fe28ef444eb7f5de6331fea6"
      },

        "text": "- Additional validation (R1-CHUNK-0184): Inject actual-result failures separately at open, body write, explicit flush, and close, with and without a prior valid result. ### Chunk0111 transfer publication build and health test checkpoint, 2026-10-09

Nine current physical path bindings saved. First combined read requested test_hud_layout184 beyondactual183 and stopped after complete transfer282-319/398-499; no unread later-path credit. Explicit corrected151-183 and all later source reads recovered; transfer499-542 separately read, union398-542 only, not whole function. Current apply gates rollback/campaign/world by phase, requires context-approved frame-boundary/all-chunks action and checksum before staging/restore. Stage checkpoint/campaign signalsready onstaged success then resets receive; world/restore/restart/rollback activates fresh reserved visit, clears pending inventory and establishes recovery/restore state before native world application, propagates success/failure through finish/status/HUD and resets. - Snapshot captures33 fields into one of12 preallocated native slots, uses identical ordered schema for direct reference and isolated worker encode/decode/reencode. pending rejects overlapping captures; discard joins pending worker before freeing pool/decoded/three buffers; worker publishes completion with release, finish observes acquire then joins. Serialization uses original epoch, copied fields and dedicated buffers, not writes to live metadata. Actual caller is AndroidD2 automation branch: reset/finish cleanup, capture/verify require live unpaused gameplay; verify writes result with checked write/close and rejects failed compare or nonadvancing GameTime64. live_changed and atomic_lock_free are reported, not asserted by caller. Worker50ms delay and clock durations are experiment instrumentation, not proof of gameplay independence or accepted speedup. Failure-path cleanup outside explicit finish/reset and actual script ownership remain to reconcile before lifecycle acceptance
- guidebot stream writes field-encoded8byte LE numbers, epoch-relative clocks, bounded counters validation even when applyfalse, textual64byte long double and bounded256byte text; apply only on current field success. writing2 measures counted bytes without I/O, but still invokes encoding/schema checks. This source alone does not prove full footer validation before live application or semantic validation of every metadata field; actual serializer consumers and ordinary tests remain required. Do not resurrect superseded flyout-history serializer from0095
- Actual save-probe branch Android only rejects unsettled/travel/transfer/paused gameplay, supports disk/memory thumbnail/blank and reusable memory modes. Measures begin/save/end, discards fresh memory, reports outside interval, checks actual write/close and final unpaused state. It is diagnostic invocation, not normal-save acceptance or measured cost evidence
- coop_autosave guards briefing/travel/restore-status/transfer, active co-op level/player/endlevel/countdown rules. It selects rotating slot, temporarily swaps game ID and callsign, invokes path save after stop_time, restores both on either result, increments slot and sends host packet only after success then writes history. No local master guard in helper; callers decide authority. Shared host abort/exit routing previously read remains a caller-specific condition. Failure pause unwind and old settled-file preservation require enclosing save path/generation owners, not comments alone. Existing0242 and0236 remain distinct; no new owner/status admitted

      },
      {
        "line": 15727,
        "text": "- Related: paired `d1/main/state.c:L874-L919`; `d2/main/state.c:L1097-L1108,L2174-L2178`; `d1/main/state.c:L784-L795`; `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/state_android_shared.c:L637-L657`; `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/android_rewind.c:L410-L441`; BR-0208 and BR-0235",

      },
      {
        "line": 15728,
        "text": "- Evidence: The D2 OGL save path allocates a 20,000-byte RGBA readback buffer and a 15,000-byte packed-RGB buffer but checks neither result. It passes `buf` directly to `glReadPixels` and then reads it and writes through `rgb` for every pixel. A failed first allocation therefore supplies a null client-memory destination to the GL driver and is subsequently dereferenced; a failed second allocation writes through null during conversion. The paired D1 helper validates its RGB allocation but likewise passes an unchecked failed 20,000-byte readback allocation to `glReadPixels` and dereferences it. The safer 200x100 Android launcher-thumbnail capture in the same files checks both allocations, demonstrating that allocation failure is expected and recoverable. BR-0208 covers the distinct blank-thumbnail fallback that silently omits bytes after a checked failure; these unchecked OGL branches crash or invoke native undefined behavior before that fallback is reached. Live D2 remains unchanged, and live D1 refactoring still leaves its readback allocation unchecked.",

      },
      {
        "line": 15729,
        "text": "- Trigger: Under OpenGL or OpenGL ES, exhaust or fault native allocation so the current-frame thumbnail's 20,000-byte readback buffer fails in either game, or its 15,000-byte RGB buffer fails in D2, then perform an ordinary non-blank manual or cooperative save",
        "line_lf_sha256": "c2292b9c2771656e728543da4c51216b53133c56b4f1ccc0847cc9d42f104986"
      },
      {
        "line": 15730,
        "text": "- Impact: Saving during memory pressure can crash inside the GL readback or conversion path, leave the destination save partially replaced, and discard the user's attempt to preserve progress. Because failure occurs after the save file is opened and header bytes are written, a prior slot can already be truncated before process termination.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "c25899bc25affee9fe7f65f5b73b266f45e6b145f72108f9b558bc41ec6d9fe9"
      },
      {
        "line": 15731,
        "text": "- Expected: Every thumbnail allocation is checked before any GL call or CPU access, and allocation failure either writes the complete fixed-width blank thumbnail or fails a staged save without replacing the prior generation.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "8af2ce22a4865c5dcd3fb9aa9e97377f9759f0ee151de6a55a0110ff4e677cfd"
      },
      {
        "line": 15732,
        "text": "- Suggested fix: Share one paired thumbnail writer that allocates and validates both buffers before changing canvas or issuing readback. On either failure, free all acquired resources, restore the prior canvas, and use a nonallocating fixed-size zero writer or propagate failure into transactional save publication. Keep launcher-cache generation best-effort only after the core thumbnail has been written successfully.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "62dea2b7ea25aed5a6144dd290458cfbfbc9be54ba7a89d3eb73325c79eeb4b1"
      },
      {
        "line": 15733,
        "text": "- Validation: Add paired allocation-fault tests at canvas, RGB, RGBA, blank-fallback, launcher-cache, body-write, and close boundaries for OGL/OGLES and software paths.         "line_lf_sha256": "666adfafe63b7fd4e579910b19eecf81f6e25bc211a7165f4bffdf849ca7e334"
      },
      {
        "line": 13452,
        "text": "- Category: correctness/multiplayer-synchronization",
        "line_lf_sha256": "d4e30ca72e57b19ab44b4cedd6f4b9821ca2c676ad3380fa1921816bb5732f2c"
      },
      {
        "line": 13453,
        "text": "- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0107, R1-CHUNK-0204, R1-CHUNK-0274",
        "line_lf_sha256": "a9bb990507b0793ddf15f222ad1e751a28f60d7d772b92e384333c82509c6e28"
      },
      {
        "line": 13454,
        "text": "- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/android_rewind.c:L398-L436` in authoritative restore and `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/multi_save_transfer.c:L188-L258,L573-L610` in client and host rewind application",
        "line_lf_sha256": "2cda2d940b5cf268c5b0fc84511fe34be17fd8763326e3b526fd4505693e5cf9"
      },
      {
        "line": 13455,
        "text": "- Related: `d1/main/state.c:L1704-L1709,L1980-L2003`, `d2/main/state.c:L2081-L2086,L2648-L2675`, and `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/state_android_shared.c:L710-L735`",
        "line_lf_sha256": "2d8e660a5d6ad74f654b00509f5aaab6cf46fdaa47153bcf3a419c29a8300dbe"
      },
      {
        "line": 13456,
        "text": "- Evidence: A cooperative rewind snapshot is serialized on the host and its save header therefore contains the host's callsign. Each client receives that buffer with `snapshot_index = -1` and calls `android_rewind_restore_authoritative`, which always calls `state_restore_from_memory`. The paired D1 and D2 restore code rejects a cooperative save whose recorded callsign differs from `Players[Player_num].callsign`; only `state_restore_coop_from_memory` enables the authoritative remap exception. Thus every normally named non-host client rejects the host snapshot before restoration. Independently, `multi_perform_rewind_request` restores the host first and only afterward calls `multi_send_rewind_save_transfer`. An active transfer or allocation failure makes that setup fail immediately, and a later ready, packet, checksum, disconnect, or timeout failure can abort it asynchronously, but the function merely logs setup failure and returns the host's successful status with no rollback. Even the success path lets the host simulate from the rewound state while clients wait for the complete transfer and apply command.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "7e40681640e19d65d130d2bac6e97e21e696459b347cfbfc94d8685516e69def"
      },
      {
        "line": 13457,
        "text": "- Trigger: In a cooperative D1 or D2 game with at least one client whose callsign differs from the host, perform a rewind; or make transfer allocation, setup, readiness, delivery, checksum, or timeout handling fail after the host selects a point",
        "line_lf_sha256": "26b37d76a4cd12f953346ae1cb635dff65eb52cbe950080c3a59cfc4443650ee"
      },
      {
        "line": 13458,
        "text": "- Impact: The host rewinds while clients remain on their prior world generation, and ordinary packets can cross between incompatible object, player, wall, RNG, and game-time states. The session can immediately desynchronize, reject subsequent state, disconnect peers, or crash in gameplay that assumes shared object identity; the advertised cooperative rewind cannot complete for the normal distinct-callsign case.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "959877c1e1fa2ec03cd6523b875a784909f17c5035193907585f4188406a7257"
      },
      {
        "line": 13459,
        "text": "- Expected: Every required peer validates and stages the same authoritative snapshot before any peer resumes from it, and all peers either apply one generation at a coordinated boundary or retain the prior state.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "e0f2d7e7b52777920ff9b88531d9a83063dfa0bc32b2380dcaa848331268bc37"
      },
      {
        "line": 13460,
        "text": "- Suggested fix: Use the cooperative authoritative restore mode for received rewind images, but make that only the apply phase of a two-phase protocol. Copy and validate the snapshot on every required peer, pause or generation-gate simulation and incompatible packets, collect readiness, then apply host and clients at one coordinated boundary and acknowledge completion. Abort before mutation if staging fails; define disconnect and apply-failure recovery rather than logging after the host has committed.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "83c7276486377883787751b98f59f84525a340ea0378a0ae2fcd37b32cdabddd"
      },
      {
        "line": 13461,
        "text": "- Validation: Run paired D1 and D2 sessions with a host and multiple distinct-callsign clients, rewind during active object, wall, score, and RNG changes, and compare complete synchronized state after resume. Inject allocation failure, an already active transfer, lost and reordered begin/chunk/apply packets, checksum mismatch, slow readiness, timeout, disconnect before each phase, and client restore failure; assert every run either applies exactly one common generation or leaves every survivor on the prior generation with no cross-generation packets.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "713c38ca07f7b2ec964d5ef434141fe42b417eb9df067500ccff4388f27bdfb8"
      },
      {
        "line": 13462,
        "text": "- Additional location (R1-CHUNK-0204): `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/multi_save_transfer.c:L215-L233,L397-L463` in cooperative save acknowledgment and host application",
        "line_lf_sha256": "ce55cb4da27320266b3f8b3bcc20052501a739abcbc5b87d4e1198e85517df1e"
      },
      {
        "line": 13463,
        "text": "- Additional evidence (R1-CHUNK-0204): The same non-atomic protocol also governs an ordinary cooperative save restore. After checksum verification, each client sends `MULTI_SAVE_TRANSFER_READY_APPLY` before `multi_prepare_restore_sync` and before calling `state_restore_coop_from_memory`. That call is fallible and mutates live state while parsing, yet the client sends no success or failure result afterward. The host records the pre-call packet as `applying_players[pnum] = 1` and, once every required slot has merely entered that branch, resets transfer state and calls its own `multi_restore_game`. A client allocation, compatibility, parse, or partial-restore failure therefore cannot veto the host: the host and successful peers commit while that client remains old or partially mutated. A client that returns failure also resets and discards its receive buffer without telling the host that application failed.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "cc3536bc6110611bfbbf2411637a209e096f6a242a102e2724e7db9d9ef45861"
      },
      {
        "line": 13464,
        "text": "- Additional validation (R1-CHUNK-0204): Cover host-selected cooperative save restoration as well as rewind in the all-peers-or-none matrix. Inject a valid-checksum image that fails parsing on exactly one client, failure before and after live mutation, delayed restore, disconnect during apply, and host local restore failure. Require a distinct staged-success acknowledgment before any mutation and a post-commit result or recoverable generation protocol; assert the host never interprets branch entry as success and every survivor either commits the same save generation or resumes the untouched prior generation.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "54fd4d38372ba230c0d9c253a51cc96830b35e384b9d86ae2e26d7a180c38054"
      },
      {
        "line": 13465,
        "text": "- Additional location (R1-CHUNK-0274): `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:d2/main/multi.c:L6824-L6852,L6915-L6962` in restore dispatch and host initiation, with `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/multi_save_transfer.c:L477-L545` in transfer setup and pending-state reporting",
        "line_lf_sha256": "857ca3e686f354097f742eec4327bebe11e548bf66751cd1176692ef60433eb4"
      },
      {
        "line": 13466,
        "text": "- Additional evidence (R1-CHUNK-0274): Every cooperative restore-transfer setup failure, including disabled packet-loss prevention, save open, size, allocation, read, or active-transfer failure, returns zero. `multi_send_restore_game` interprets that zero as permission to broadcast the legacy `MULTI_RESTORE_GAME` packet, and `multi_initiate_restore_game` then observes no active pending transfer and immediately calls `multi_restore_game` on the host. The legacy packet carries only a slot and game ID, not the host's authoritative save image; with per-player save namespaces, peers can lack or reject that local slot while the host has already committed. Thus a setup failure that should abort before mutation instead starts a host-only generation and exposes the same cross-generation traffic and failure modes as the later apply failures already tracked here.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "be1fecc411617ee3d14384cb52e4520250951d4469339c692156a48c04d22fe2"
      },
      {
        "line": 13467,
        "text": "- Additional validation (R1-CHUNK-0274): In paired cooperative restore tests, inject each setup failure before any begin packet: packet-loss prevention disabled, missing or unreadable host save, zero and oversized file, allocation and short-read failure, and an already active transfer. Require no legacy restore packet, no host or client state mutation, no score or object traffic from a new generation, an explicit failure result, and a cleared or recoverable transfer state; retain the no-connected-client case as the only path allowed to restore locally without a transfer.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "374854abc7f0c560bf6d21394e5983b7f1a4615add1fdd750fc4e81b298ae38a"
      },
      {
        "line": 13468,
        "text": "- Resolution: Pending",
        "line_lf_sha256": "9283e8d2b02a60dd95afcd32c737e52c949ba2cc15180e9d8967d03ca1e1d976"
      },
      {
        "line": 13469,
        "text": "",
        "line_lf_sha256": "01ba4719c80b6fe911b091a7c05124b64eeece964e09c058ef8f9805daca546b"
      }
    ]
  }
]

### Chunk0113 paired caller and ordinary fixture checkpoint, 2026-10-09

- Ten current physical paths bound below; selected ranges read completely without truncation. Recovered config continuations, pilot mirror predicates/wrappers and autonet host/join continuation from the prior interrupted read. Only two fixture files have whole-current physical credit here; discovery searches and frozen reads add none
- D1 config333-405/D2config354-428: saved-pilot helper receives engine-owned callsign/LastPlayer arrays, and borrowed result is consumed by PHYSFSX_printf before function return. Graphics lock released on open failure and after close; write results and PHYSFS_close result are not checked. Both pilot wrappers ignore WriteConfigFile result, return primary write result and ignore optional saved-pilot mirror result; mirror occurs only after primary EZERO and transient-current/real-saved predicate. Existing persistence/transaction canonical owner binding remains required; no new finding/status admitted
- Shared auto-join109-163 restores selected host route and adjusts temporary Player_num if it equals migrated master before actual join. Auto-host170-236 loads mission before validating level/mode/difficulty/maxplayers, but validates before opening/resetting network state. Briefing/secret-warp options are cooperative-only. Do not interpret network prevalidation comment as no mission/world mutation on failed launch
- Paired endlevel D1 4770-4820/D2 4905-4955: exact extent short-circuits before packet byte reads, validates type/token, host index and sender IP or master IP before introspection helper; WAITING diverts to score catchup before probe; world-fence allowed predicate calculated before probe and disallowed packets return before clocks/state parsing. Full authenticated transport/stamp semantics, N_players invariant and probe completion/injection consumers remain pending
- Paired initial-sync send D1 6284-6310/D2 6462-6488: connected nonself peers get sync then retry arm(timer_query,UDP_TIMEOUT); playing reconnect branch calls should_resend before prepare/re-send. Authentication caller context, complete branch, reset/confirmation, fixed-point timeout definitions and generation behavior remain pending
- Whole retry fixture41 lines checks unarmed reset, arm at start and inclusive deadline, deadline+1 rejection, confirmation, invalid indices. Whole WAV fixture65 lines exercises mono/stereo eight/sixteen-bit PCM conversion including signed endpoint values and caller free, invalid input/output null, null encoded input and encoded cap. No malformed/resource-pressure/runtime acceptance inferred. CMake selected ranges show SDL_FOUND conditional WAV executable/link/add_test, retry target and host-list entry plus add_test foreach; complete host-list definition remains to read before registration gate closure
- Read-only discovery corrected nonexistent root CMakeLists.txt to android/tests/CMakeLists.txt; discovery is not physical coverage. No source/test/script edits or build/test/device/network/media/security/allocation execution. All four remaining plan gates stay open, goal active. Next complete paired retry reset/confirmation/time definitions and auth/preflight callers, WAV consumer/SDL allocation lifetime, autonet producer/control flow and maintained integration fixtures, then canonical bindings/report/audit

        "text": "- Validation: Add paired D1 and D2 protocol tests with separate host, sender, victim, and observer identities; cover valid self-warp, host restoration and host difficulty changes, valid and throttled client rewind, non-host restore and difficulty forgery, mismatched peer-status, warp, and rewind identities, rewind slot cycling, forged outer and inner slots, arbitrary warp segment and coordinates, host relay, direct and reliable delivery, stale restoration outside rejoin, and boundary plus invalid record fields.         "text": "- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/playsave_android_shared.c:L145-L170,L202-L209,L241-L248,L286-L300,L325-L413`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/NativePilotPreferences.kt:L174-L220,L249-L294,L311-L357`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/EnginePreferencesPage.kt:L338-L363,L443-L471`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/GraphicsSettingsPage.kt:L543-L570`, and `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/ConfigImportExport.kt:L360-L400`",

      {
        "line": 13844,
        "text": "- Evidence: Each assigned per-file writer accurately returns the result of one transactional replacement, but the bridge destroys that failure information when one UI action spans fields or files. D1's engine visitor performs separate cockpit and robot-count replacements and returns `cockpit_result || counts_result`, so either half can fail after the other commits and the file is still counted as successful. D2 patches binary cockpit, auto-level, and headlight fields separately from text robot counts, then reports `max(plr_total, plx_total)`, hiding failures or missing counterparts on either side. Every `for_each_pilot` loop sums only successful visitors and never reports how many matching files were discovered or which failed. Kotlin then adds game totals or takes another `max`; the engine and graphics pages treat any positive count as complete success, copy all requested values into their saved state, persist mirrored preferences, and display \"Saved\" even when another field, pilot, or game remained unchanged. The single-file transaction test cannot detect this grouped partial commit.",

      },

        "text": "- Trigger: Have multiple D1 or D2 pilots, or one D1 pilot with both `.plr` and `.plx`, then make one target unreadable, exceed the text size limit, inject allocation, write, sync, close, or replace failure for one field or file, or remove one binary/text counterpart while saving launcher engine, visual, homing, or music preferences",
        "line_lf_sha256": "3134b3959a01da52a26c5b72d44f1641adbf8cf670fb0af0887d6dd9152dd648"
      },
      {
        "line": 13846,
        "text": "- Impact: A nominal app-wide save can leave pilots and paired binary/text settings split across old and new values while the launcher reports success and clears its dirty state. Later game selection, export, or launch can load a different value than the UI claims was saved, and retry is not prompted because failure is indistinguishable from a smaller successful pilot set.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "3c46cbb2df75f8b8c3b4600c21eb9453de3a184924ab8740ca4b0b04a09b3d6f"
      },
      {
        "line": 13847,
        "text": "- Expected: An app-wide preference operation either commits the complete requested field set to every discovered target or reports a precise partial failure without advancing saved UI or mirrored preference state; a missing required counterpart is explicit rather than folded into a positive count.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "e66d6d473b412d4786d37db0ef3ac22dbbf2428e868bb97146611c88fe84c298"
      },
      {
        "line": 13848,
        "text": "- Suggested fix: Enumerate and validate the complete target set first, preserve discovered, staged, committed, and failed identities in a structured result, and stage every per-file replacement before publication. For fields sharing one text file, update them in one section transaction. Publish all staged files with rollback or recoverable backups, and let Kotlin mark saved state only when every required target committed; otherwise show exact failed pilots and retain the dirty state.",
        "line_lf_sha256": "4f37c015a5f76ee25080bce4fe0dfb06993f7c5d0ca0f549057d85d636442424"
      }
    ]

Native death-frame owns camera, timed explosion, hostage clearing/status publication, capped eggs, multiplayer explode notification and conversion to ghost. The abort path drops once if needed then calls DoPlayerDead. Native DoPlayerDead ends the death sequence, records multiplayer death or decrements singleplayer lives, preserves destroyed-reactor advancement and initializes/starts a new ship otherwise. D2 holds death during travel and keeps intact cooperative secret mines on ordinary respawn; singleplayer secret restore/return and D1-in-D2 completion remain separate engine policy. Pickup gating waits for live provenance; accounting subtracts actual before/after inventory gains and retains overflow credit. The native explosion-send tails encode life/omega, send before recovery_drop and then clear the created-object list. Preserve these ownership/order boundaries, not an alternate fixture-specific inventory algorithm

## Native damage, contents release, boss/reactor and key contact checkpoint

Fivecurrentphysicalnativepaths/14bounded ranges actuallyread and freshlyhashed below. LiveHEADa55f2a759e71da814f59497e3ed80bd4143cf0ad unchanged. No wholefile or entireexplosion/pickup-function credit; complete contextual deltas pending

Whole apply_damage_to_controlcen rejects nonplayer killer/invalid object, respects native multiplayer invulnerability, subtracts shields, invokes do_controlcen_destroyed_stuff before explosion/score. Whole robotdamage rejects exploding/alreadydead, preserves importedD1boss hook, native companion/finalboss restrictions, then starts boss/robot deathroll or delayed explosion. Controller uses stationary ConsoleObject as native killer and localGM_NORMAL, so no claim that calling damage bypasses every native lifecycle or network policy

Native authored robotcontains_count releases through delayed explosion spawn into object_create_egg/drop_powerup from actual sourcevelocity/pose/segment. Random robot-info contents are distinct SIM RNG branch; shield/energy resource suppression does not generally suppress native keys. ImportedD1 resource/count initialization remains engine-owned. Actual key object arrival/contact can occur after carrier negative shields and is required by controller; do not simplify to immediate keyflag mutation or complete objective solely on damage. Selected explosion prefix does not establish entire deletion/allocation failure lifecycle

Whole boss deathroll routine waits native time and then invokes do_controlcen_destroyed_stuff(NULL)/explosion. Whole finalboss countdown additionally requires Final_boss_is_dead plusControl_center_destroyed, two native seconds before confirmation interception; normal start_endlevel remains after interceptor. Finalboss hacks preserve local death/shield/invulnerability handling and setdead flag. Reactor destruction validates linkedwalls, toggles native walls, marksdestroyed/resets pause, updates Android route notification and secret-companionfile, installs authored/difficulty/importedcountdown. Explicitpause rejects inactive/expired timers; controller's forcedexpired pause is isolatedroute-proof behavior, not new general reactorAPI

Native local playerpowerup contact rejects observer/dead/endlevel/nonlocal player, retains Android recovery/duplication admission and invokes do_powerup. Blue/red/gold currentflag and nativeaccessmessage update ownership lies in powerup.c; key is consumed in singleplayer, preserved in multiplayer, and routekey invalidation stays native. Selected coopremote branch read only as context, not a wholefunction/network proof. Preserve contact/currentflag distinction from carrier death and emittedshot versus directdamage proofscope

## Ordinary saved-world, explicit-key, native-transition and lifecycle fixture checkpoint

Seven whole current ordinary fixtures (370 lines), the whole 93-line integration owner and whole 107-line case catalog were freshly read without truncated-output credit. Current coverage/master registration, selection and timeout ranges were read separately. Complete current deltas for all 11 source-context paths were read: nine empty, coverage 103 lines and master 111 lines. Saved-world envelope metadata was inspected without displaying its compressed payload; in-memory-only decoding proves declared 373995 bytes and SHA256, not successful native restore or execution. All range/raw/delta fingerprints follow below

Saved-world fixture repeats isolated restored L9 requests, requires saved pose segment138, blue flag2, difficulty0, CONFIRMED/nonzero frames/full player radius, no authored-start certificate and identical complete result hashes. It rejects a mismatched L10 checkpoint with process exit1/no result, and checks input integrity. A serial child pool records timeout and process status. These witnesses preserve saved-world semantics; they do not test repeated session start, publication failures or every restored field

Explicit-key fixture stages Lost Levels L4, earns blue through native route confirmation, writes a checkpoint and restores it. Earned pickup requires nonzero frames and blue-key objective; already-carried restored blue may confirm at zero frames with flag2/segment83. Missing gold requires failed zero-frame result/exit2/no output checkpoint. Each result pair is hash-compared and the input save remains unchanged. Explicit key completion is narrower than mine completion

Secret-transition fixture uses the earned blue checkpoint and repeats native entry4->-1 trigger20, return-1->4 trigger0 and revisit4->-1 trigger20. Every case requires actual from/to transition, preserved blue flag2, enter_exit activation, nonzero frames/full radius/no authored certificate, a nonempty output checkpoint and unchanged input. Native secret.sgb/secret.sgc existence and revisit persistence hash are distinct witnesses. Full result hashes must repeat. Preserve these native handoff assertions instead of treating an intercepted exit log alone as level transition

Counterstrike L17 requires the exact eight-objective sequence including blue carrier and exit, then compares frames and simulation RNG state/calls across two results. L10 requests two repeats but inspects first-run labels/status plus normalized level status; its body does not independently compare both raw results. L24 requires two CONFIRMED results whose last objective is Exit and compares frames/RNG; it does not independently assert final-boss death flags or a native level transition. These are controller/native-lifecycle acceptance oracles, not ordinary unrestricted combat proof

Crossfire L15 requires the exact key/reactor/exit sequence twice, the expired-countdown sandbox log, no AddressSanitizer/runtime-error log match, identical raw results and normalized ok status with zero countdown, >=7 measured escape seconds and one insufficient-time advisory. The advisory remains separate from physical isolated completion and ordinary countdown feasibility

Five support fixtures belong to test_guidebot_route_regressions and have Always=false catalog entries. Normal selection runs canaries plus one sorted case per family per seed; -AllCases selects all. The owner builds once if needed, invokes each selected child serially with 600-second pool timeout, records timeout/process exit/log and atomic summary, and propagates declared skips separately. Master gives this owner 1800 seconds normally or7200 for FullRouteCorpus. Saved-world and secret-transition are separately registered in saved_routes and no-infrastructure classification; that family rotates normally and is included in all-scenarios selection

Observed acceptance gap for owner reconciliation: standalone saved-world/secret-transition have no explicit master timeout override in the complete402-492 table; their entries therefore retain zero and Invoke-Test uses the configurable master default (declared120). Saved-world children allow300 seconds each, with180-second simulation requests, while secret transition includes staging and multiple native requests. This is a source-proven mismatch of declared allowance, not a measured timeout failure or newly admitted defect. Existing test infrastructure/publication owners must be revalidated before assigning remediation. Likewise explicit-key/secret-transition use Windows .exe and a fixed data path unlike the saved-world platform resolver. Preserve observations for shared test-owner reconciliation; do not introduce a duplicate root or claim runtime results

It rearms a previously fired action only when its effect is needed and it targets a changed shootable wall; consumed one-shot is a separate veto. Non-navigation actions take fire-only return. Visibility chooses conditional/native wall callback or target callback, distinguishes current pose from center cache, and separates detailed near-face samples by sample_kind. Namespace/target wall or target segment/position is the cache key; ownership must bind it to the actual query/snapshot/radius/destroyed-state lifetime before asserting reuse. Detailed samples include face, vertex and edge midpoints; count limits skip new cache insertions. Source discovery validates source eligibility and uses vector-valued trigger actions, supports unexposed/direct-trigger discovery and excludes lock/unlock-only reverse targets. Ordinary scene/schema preconditions and all-opener topology construction require actual producer trace

Search now allocates seven entry states per segment (six sides plus canonical), tracks closed/parent/heap nodes by state, and projects best state per segment for target selection. Narrow portal transit uses reverse entry plus nonzero compiled transit-exit masks; current entry masks filter exits. Reconstruct via state parent and saved incoming edge so repeated segment entries retain obstruction identity. Do not collapse to segment-only Dijkstra or copy parent fields without preserving masks/state ancestry. Ordinary central geometry distance remains heuristic; graph reachability is not physical acceptance by itself

Target selection ranks progress then distance then identity; key acquisition search forbids requiring the missing key and ranks distance rather than progress. Switch guidance compiles passable strong components using iterative DFS/reverse traversal, retaining optimistic edges but excluding clearance-insufficient direct edges. Trigger selection charges each dependency search, prefers local reachable/shootable pose before remote prerequisite expansion, and groups guidance candidates by segment with utility and independent initial-start utility. Shot distanceweight4 and incidence penalty (cos75degrees floor0.01) prefer useful near/square firing poses while retaining confirmed steep shots; approximate/confirmed/steep quality remains explicit. Candidate quality and utility are metadata, not actual emitted shot or physical completion proof

The assigned boundary ends inside firing-position selection. Fresh enclosing1762-1770 begins downstream region-ranking block but does not complete the function; broader source and dependency callers must be read or exactly bound audited prior evidence before credit. Initial observations include existing geometry signed arithmetic and state-vector assumptions; ordinary producer bounds and existing owners must be checked before any defect claim. No malformed, allocation or security probes; no builds/tests/execution/source changes

## Native snapshot, transit/action producers and public cache-budget contracts checkpoint

Six current physical source contexts/22 bounded ranges freshly read and hashed below. Whole route_planner.h382 and trigger_navigation_actions.h74 were actually read; other paths receive bounded-context credit. Complete current deltas read: five empty and secretarea81 lines, which change metadata save capture/deferred serialization rather than the selected geometry/trigger producers. LiveHEAD and assigned planner raw identity revalidated. Source-only, no execution

Snapshot build validates finite native count ceilings before vector materialization and requires adjacency. Every topology/state wall and trigger vector is created to the same view count; action/link counts are checked. Transit callbacks are masked to six bits; absent callback leaves topology defaults0x3f. Source position, side centers/clearance, all-opener vectors, trigger ordered actions/one-shot/disabled, current wall kind/key/lock/opening, contained keys and current object positions are captured separately. Topology hash includes vertices, transit masks, adjacency/reverse/clearance/openers, ordered trigger actions/link identities and actual reveal-pattern flag. Ordinary generated snapshot has aligned topology/state vectors, so direct per-wall state reads are not evidence of an ordinary size mismatch by themselves

Actual switch reveal flag requires a shootable source whose current kind is open, an opener source action, and a close-wall action linked directly or via the reciprocal wall. Potential open/close pairs with an existing surface retain legacy behavior. Preserve this native snapshot-derived selection; do not make every ordinary level use stateful reveal planning merely to simplify a branch

Native secret_area_segment_transit_passable requires valid distinct entry/exit child sides and selected clearance radius, offsets side centers inward, verifies actual segment membership, and performs full-radius FVI with a geometry-portal callback. That callback accepts adjacency regardless of actual wall access: these masks describe geometry, while evaluate_route_edge independently owns key/door/progression access. Transit-mask producer excludes compiled narrow portals and admits center-fitting or either-direction traversable paths. Portal-too-narrow uses actual solid intersection and native edge tolerance, preserving open-room subdivisions. Topology rebuild sets the selected radius, classifies small isolated bad-center components, compiles portal/segment clearance and starts the all-opener index. This read ends at2705 inside index construction; no whole all-opener producer or full rebuild credit

Native trigger_navigation_actions whole header supports D1 and D1-in-D2 ordered multiple actions, terminal exit precedence and native toggle meaning. It intentionally strips one-shot consumption from native D1/imported D1 navigation flags because native repeated crossings remain admitted after ON clearing; actual D2 TF_ONE_SHOT remains distinct. Per-trigger action/link callback forwarding and D1/D2 type mapping were actually read. Do not infer a one-shot defect from D1 flags alone or consolidate vector actions to one enum

The whole public planner header makes state_nodes/best_state_by_segment, ordered trigger vectors, guidance quality/incidence/candidates and default legacy complete_trigger_effects=false visible. Public direct C++ callers may supply an optional analysis budget/cache; source-level default{} is distinct from native exported wrappers. Native planner wrappers5255-5416 and5418-5473 were completely read in bounded ranges. They build the snapshot inside try, own a per-call visibility cache and2000000 work/65536 cache-entry budget, bind cancellation, then plan/project. This is real bounded-work/cache ownership to preserve, not evidence of a missing cache lifetime across ordinary calls

Opaque-shot optional alternative copies remaining budget and increments namespace. Approximate shots use0x80000000; conditional before/after predicted reactor state uses0x40000000/0x60000000. Those modes were actually traced in selected dependency caller4124-4168 and wrapper5339-5374. Cache lifetime is per native request; namespace distinguishes changed shot policy. Ordinary lifetime/mode controls must be checked before claiming stale-cache reuse solely because radius or snapshot is absent from the sample key

Budget outcomes are intentionally different: main planning may project a meaningful work-exhausted partial route and return1 with PARTIAL/problem; cancellation returns0; optional opaque alternative exhaustion can retain an already completed main route while propagating cancellation; segment-reachable returnsfalse if cancelled/exhausted and catches all exceptions. Preserve truthful route status/partial provenance and producer exceptions rather than replacing every budget event with generic success/failure. Snapshot construction precedes planner budget creation, and geometry graph/search allocations still need whole-attempt shared admission reconciliation; existingGQR0212/GQR0173 context must be read before owner extension. These readings do not execute allocation/work/cancellation failure tests

Next: finish complete firing selection and actual dependency entry/caller ownership as needed, inspect maintained snapshot fixtures for transit-state reconstruction, stable ordering, ordered contrary/one-shot actions/reveal and cache-budget policy, then canonical owner/minimization reconciliation and publication. Gate2 remains pending for caller completion; gates3-5 pending. Canonical281DONE346TODO unchanged; no newroot/rerating/closure or code/test/helper edits

## Helper ownership, completion replacement and checkpoint overflow candidate

Fresh helper reads now bind occupancy memoization, scan-view refresh/profile construction, all visibility checkpoint helpers, complete compiled-step preparation/restorer/access/alternative-exit helpers and compiled selector. Current-source coverage and partial frozen matches are fingerprinted below. The completed native helper range790-1457 is not whole certifier reading and does not discharge unrelated certifier chunks. Full current deltas were freshly read for paired main build lists, headless helper, Android CMake and listed unchanged fixtures. The earlier combined build/snapshot-delta output was truncated and is not accepted; new snapshot fixture has actual whole-current reading but no complete-delta read claim.

Occupancy is an independent direct-mapped memo of geometric point/size validity, with no consume_fvi call. Hash collisions replace an entry only after full key comparison. This eliminates the suspected occupancy budget-rejection mechanism, but segmented visibility credibility can still consume native collision work; budget-negative cache admission remains a distinct caller reconciliation. Actor clearance refresh uses maximum player/navigator radius for topology and native start/current keys/reactor state for scan. Profile adds D1 content semantics inside D2, navigator/projectile radius and shot-model version.

Checkpoint loading checks chunk length, magic, sequence, count, identity and checksum before replay; close is independent of read outcome, unlike BR-0336. Loading suppresses recursive checkpoint writes and excludes pose-cache records. Existing entry rewrites are not appended as new durable samples; do not infer a universal last-write-wins journal from this format. Completion discards sample files only after the canonical route has been successfully saved complete (checkpoint3 caller). Failed optional sample persistence must not undermine planner correctness or memory safety.

NEW PROPOSED ROOT, not yet canonically admitted: flush returns without resetting pending count on directory/open/write/close/rename failure. Pending chunk has256 entries. Store sees count>=256, retries flush, reloads count, then unconditionally writes entries[count] without checking remaining capacity. After the256th sample fills the buffer and flush fails, a257th newly admitted sample with another failed flush writes entries[256], outside the static array. Later writes can continue beyond it. Current native source and frozen source contain this same path. Default persistent cache is enabled; Android analysis JNI1288 reaches rescan3936/checkpoint_load and cache-store823, so a valid cache key plus sufficiently many unique samples under persistent storage failure reaches the condition. Successful retry resets count and avoids it; non-Android normal loading does not establish key validity. Canonical search of quality/open/done BR ledgers for the exact helper/buffer and visibility checkpoint terms finds zero matches. This is distinct from BR-0336 handle leakage. No runtime test/repro was run and no finding/investigation ID has been allocated. Next admission must reconcile broad memory ownerGQR0212 against this concrete bounds-after-failed-flush root; do not hide it under a retained migration or claim no new defects.

Proposed minimal repair is a capacity recheck after flush before any write, with bounded retry/backpressure policy for optional sample caching and explicit diagnostics. Preserve valid pending/prior samples or disable further optional admission safely; never let storage failure increase count past capacity. Acceptance must exercise actual helper through injected mkdir/open/short-write/close/rename failures at255/256/257 and repeated retries, successful retry reset, normal multi-chunk replay, sanitizer bounds and continuing planner fallback. Inline source reasoning is diagnosis, not executed fault coverage.

The four retired adapter names are replaced by shared ordered trigger navigation and current world predicates/compiled selection, rather than a positional completion-bit array. Fresh world-required function180-292 skips held keys and destroyed reactor/boss objectives; triggered/disabled one-shots stay complete, repeatable close effects depend on current wall state, activated traversal triggers stay complete after auto-close, hidden/guided doors use visited/passability policy. D2 guidebot1755-1787 latches actual trigger activation and updates event generation; reset478 clears latch at route reset, save member282 serializes it. Native D2 switch532 and695 notify after accepted native-D1 or D2 trigger handling. These source associations establish ownership replacement; they do not prove every paired effect/coop/restore boundary or close BR-0335/publication owners.

Compiled selector now tests required current actions, switch-surface validity/restoration and reachable guidance; preparation may select an alternative same-destination-type exit or access trigger. Approximate fallback is guidance, not fresh physical shot certification. BFS/trigger/wall scans are bounded by engine arrays but the wrapper ignores supplied2ms/work512 budget; preserve separate outer-deadline acceptance. Retain source identity and effect confirmation owners. Synthetic certifier fixture535-768 actually checks collected-key skip, missing surface rejection, restoring-PENDING transition, restorer selection, one-shot/disabled completion after reopen, moved key-object binding and reactor firing segment. This is synthetic callback coverage, not paired engine save/activation/collision acceptance.

Current native runtime5316-5405 keeps versioned identity reader/writer, validated matching level identity and visited legacy restoration; D2 native-D1 identity translation is gated by proven original level identity.
